conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: Morning, let’s start with Project Falcon, the backend migration to Azure. Where are we on readiness and who’s on point this week?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: Morning. We’re about 80% to environment parity. Ken is leading the cloud setup with two engineers. Biggest items left are Security’s review on logging and Finance approving the Azure credits.

conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: Got it. What’s our next milestone and target date?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: Parity checklist by Jan 20, then a full dry run late next week. If that goes well, we aim for a Feb 1-2 cutover window, ideally Saturday night.

conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: How much customer impact during the cutover? We’ll need to prep Comms and Support.

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: We’re planning for near-zero, but we’ll announce a 60-minute maintenance window to be safe. Support runbook and status page draft need Luis’s sign-off.

conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: Any dependencies we haven’t surfaced?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: Okta integration for admin logins, data residency confirmation from Legal, and a final checkpoint with our Azure rep, Toby, on reserved instances pricing.

conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: What about resourcing — do you need more hands?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: One more cloud engineer contractor for two weeks would help us finish hardening without pulling people off bug fixes. Also an Azure credits top-up to avoid throttling in the dry run.

conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: Switching to Project Orion — the AI integration for customer support. What’s the plan for the first slice and who’s involved?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: We’ll start with suggested replies and smarter routing in the agent console. Luis’s team will provide labeled examples; Priya from Data Science will help with evaluation. Legal and Privacy want to review data flows.

conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: Timeline-wise, what are the key milestones?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: Data mapping by Jan 22, training set freeze Jan 29, internal pilot with 10% of tickets starting Feb 5. We’ll monitor CSAT, handle time, and first-contact resolution.

conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: What’s our deflection and satisfaction target for the pilot?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: We’re conservatively aiming for a 10-15% improvement in handle time and no drop in CSAT. Anything that’s uncertain will route to a human with a clear flag.

conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: Do we need budget or tools to support this?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: We need about 40 agent-hours for labeling next week, plus vendor sandbox credits. Finance needs to approve a modest increase this quarter.

conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: Any risks beyond privacy?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: Two: agent adoption if suggestions feel off, and policy alignment. We’re drafting guardrails with Luis, including an easy thumbs down for bad suggestions and a no-automation path for sensitive cases.

conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: Let’s talk Project Zenith, the new mobile feature. Where do we stand?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: Design is locked, and the iOS work is underway. On Android, we need another Java-heavy developer to keep pace. Code complete target is Jan 25.

conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: What are the downstream milestones?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: Beta build to internal testers Jan 29, app store submission Feb 3, staged rollout starting Feb 10, and general availability Feb 17 if metrics look good.

conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: Any external dependencies?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: We’re waiting on Marketing for final copy and screenshots, and Legal needs to approve the new terms blurb. Also a minor dependency on the payments SDK update — we’ve asked the vendor to confirm compatibility.

conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: How’s QA capacity with Falcon’s dry run overlapping?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: Tight. Marco’s team is covering both. If Falcon’s dry run stays on the 27th, we’ll shift Zenith’s beta a day to avoid burning out the testers.

conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: Resource asks?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: One Android contractor for two weeks, and a few hours of localization support from Sofia so we don’t slip non-English markets.

conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: Quick Falcon check-in — parity was due by Jan 20. Did we make it?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: We reached 95%. Security flagged log retention settings; we’re adjusting today. Finance is still reviewing the Azure credits, but Toby offered temporary promo credits to cover the dry run.

conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: Is the Feb 1 cutover still realistic?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: Yes, if we clear Security by Thursday and get Support’s runbook sign-off from Luis by Friday. Dry run is scheduled Jan 27, 9-11 PM.

conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: We should draft customer communications now. Can you give Comms a one-pager?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: Absolutely. I’ll include the 60-minute window, rollback plan at a high level, and contact points.

conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: How does this affect Orion’s data freeze on the 29th?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: No direct block. We’ll freeze support data snapshots independent of the migration. Priya is aligned, and we’ll avoid running heavy data exports during the dry run.

conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: And Zenith? You mentioned shifting beta if needed.

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: I talked to Marco. We’ll move Zenith’s beta to Jan 30 to leave QA headroom on the 27th. Jules on the mobile team is okay with that.

conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: Orion update — how did data mapping go, and are we on track for tomorrow’s training set freeze?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: Mapping is complete. We validated the key categories with Luis’s supervisors. Training set freeze is on for Jan 29. Privacy review with Maya and Chen is booked for Thursday.

conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: Do we have the agent training plan for the pilot?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: Yes. Short videos and an FAQ. We’ll do 30-minute sessions with each shift on Feb 4 so they’re ready for the Feb 5 pilot.

conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: Budget-wise, are we okay on labeling hours and vendor credits?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: Labeling is at 70% complete; we need one more day of agent time. Vendor invoice went to Raj yesterday for sign-off.

conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: Switching briefly to Falcon: how did the dry run last night go?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: Mostly smooth. We saw a longer-than-expected DNS propagation in one region, adding about 12 minutes to the window. We updated the runbook and will start the comms clock earlier in the real cutover.

conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: Any change to the Feb 1 plan?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: No date change. We’ll widen the announced window to 90 minutes for safety, but still target under an hour. Support is aligned on messaging.

conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: Big week. First, Falcon — how did the Feb 1 cutover go in the end?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: We completed in 48 minutes with about 20 minutes of read-only mode. No customer tickets about downtime. We have a short post-mortem Thursday and plan to decommission the legacy environment by Feb 15.

conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: Great news. Any follow-ups we need to communicate to stakeholders?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: Yes, a thank-you and the final runbook in Confluence. Elena from Ops and Martina from Security want the audit artifact. Also, Toby asked for feedback for the Azure case study.

conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: On Orion — pilot starts tomorrow. Any last-mile concerns?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: Agent training wrapped today. We added stronger guardrails based on Privacy feedback. The pilot is limited to billing and password reset categories, with clear escalation if confidence is low.

conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: Success metrics still CSAT hold and 10-15% handle time improvement?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: Correct. Plus we’ll track opt-out rates. We’ll review early results on Feb 7 and decide whether to extend to 25% of tickets on Feb 12.

conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: And Zenith — did we get the app submitted on Feb 3?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: Yes, both platforms submitted. We’re waiting on review. Staged rollout still planned for Feb 10, pending crash-free rate thresholds and Marketing’s campaign assets from Nina.

conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: Midweek check. For Orion, what did we see in the Feb 7 review, and are we ready to ramp?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: Early results are encouraging: handle time down about 12% in the pilot categories, CSAT stable, opt-out around 8%. Escalation rules worked as planned. We propose ramping to 25% today, and Luis is on board.

conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: Any stakeholder pushback on the ramp plan?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: Privacy signed off. Legal asked for a small tweak to the in-product disclaimer. Marketing prefers we describe it as smart assistance rather than using AI as a label.

conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: Falcon decommission still slated for Feb 15?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: Yes. Backups verified, observability is healthy, and Finance approved reserved instances. We’re seeing early signs of cost savings compared to the legacy setup.

conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: How’s Zenith’s staged rollout since Feb 10?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: Live at 10% on Android and 5% on iOS. Crash-free rate at 99.4%. We patched one edge-case bug in onboarding. QA says we can go to 25% tomorrow if metrics hold.

conversation.speaker: Dave
conversation.message: Do we have enough support coverage and marketing alignment for a wider mobile release?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.message: Luis added weekend coverage, and Nina scheduled a light push notification. We’ll keep a close eye on app store reviews and be ready to pause the ramp if sentiment dips.

questions.question: What were the key milestones and target dates for Project Falcon?
questions.answer: Environment parity by Jan 20, a dry run on Jan 27 (9-11 PM), the production cutover on Feb 1-2 with a 60-90 minute window, and legacy decommission by Feb 15.

questions.question: Which stakeholders were identified for Project Orion and what metrics were used to assess the pilot?
questions.answer: Stakeholders included Luis (Support), Priya (Data Science), Maya and Chen (Legal and Privacy). The pilot was assessed by CSAT, handle time improvement (target 10-15%), first-contact resolution, and opt-out rates.

questions.question: Why was Zenith’s beta date shifted, and what were the revised milestones?
questions.answer: It was shifted to avoid QA overload due to Falcon’s dry run. Revised milestones were beta on Jan 30, app store submission on Feb 3, staged rollout from Feb 10, and GA targeted for Feb 17 pending metrics.

questions.question: What resource requests did Sarah make across the three projects?
questions.answer: For Falcon: one cloud engineer contractor and Azure credits top-up. For Orion: about 40 agent-hours for labeling and vendor sandbox credits. For Zenith: one Android (Java) contractor and a few hours of localization support.

questions.question: What risks were identified for Project Orion and how were they mitigated?
questions.answer: Risks included privacy concerns, agent adoption, and policy alignment. Mitigations were Privacy and Legal reviews, guardrails and disclaimers, limited pilot scope to specific categories, easy escalation to human agents, and agent training.

questions.question: How did the actual Falcon cutover go compared to the plan?
questions.answer: It completed in 48 minutes with about 20 minutes of read-only mode, within the announced window, with no customer tickets about downtime. A post-mortem was scheduled and decommission planned for Feb 15.

questions.question: What early results did the team see from the Orion pilot and what was the next step?
questions.answer: Handle time down about 12%, CSAT stable, opt-out around 8%, escalation working. The next step was to ramp from 10% to 25% of tickets on Feb 12, with stakeholder approval.
